channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Building-block synthesis as a determinant of antibiotic persistence
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78277-3

Reduced antibiotic target activity is a major driver of antibiotic treatment failure. While this has mostly been linked to the presence of low-energy bacteria, a recent study by Taher and colleagues suggests that reduced building-block synthesis can also promote antibiotic survival during nitrogen starvation — a route distinct from energy limitation.
item.dc:title: Building-block synthesis as a determinant of antibiotic persistence

item.title: Environmental stochasticity reduces human planning effort
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78023-9

The real world is stochastic, making it difficult to know when planning is worthwhile. Here the authors show that as stochasticity increases, people spend less effort planning and adopt simpler, less value-sensitive decision policies.
item.dc:title: Environmental stochasticity reduces human planning effort

item.title: mHolmes improves cross anatomical cadaveric microbiome forecasting for postmortem interval estimation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77510-3

This study presents mHolmes, a transfer-learning framework that forecasts postmortem microbiome changes across body sites, improving postmortem interval estimation and highlighting microbial features with forensic potential.

item.title: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78159-8

Tungsten-dependent enzyme production is limited by complex metal cofactor requirements and poor compatibility with expression hosts. Here the authors engineer E. coli to support the aerobic production of various tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases.
item.dc:title: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli

item.title: Nighttime warming dominates the thermal evolution of lakes across China
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78114-7

A 25-year analysis of 613 Chinese lakes shows that lake warming is largely driven by nighttime temperature increases, with atmospheric longwave radiation and human activities reinforcing this trend.
item.dc:title: Nighttime warming dominates the thermal evolution of lakes across China

item.title: “Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition”
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77949-4

The neural control of LUT (lower urinary tract) function is not fully understood. Here authors demonstrate that transcriptionally distinct enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus are recruited during voiding to selectively control external urethral sphincter relaxation and regulate urinary behaviors in a sex-specific manner.
item.dc:title: “Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition”
